queries.title: Search queries
queries.description: Keywords to search for. Leave empty to browse by tag/date only (e.g. latest front-page stories or the newest Who's Hiring thread), or when using author/usernames/domainFilter/excludeKeywords/a points-comments-date filter to browse by those instead of a text query.

tags.title: Filter by tag
tags.description: story, comment, poll, ask_hn, show_hn, job, front_page. Listing several tags returns items matching ANY of them (they are OR-ed): ["story","comment"] returns both stories and comments, ["story"] alone returns posts only.

includeComments.title: Include comments
includeComments.description: If tags includes 'comment', set true to fetch comment text too. Set false to drop comments; if 'comment' is the only tag you asked for, the run is skipped with a warning rather than silently widening the search to every other content type.

sortBy.title: Sort order
sortBy.description: 'relevance' ranks by search relevance and points; 'date' returns the newest items first.

minPoints.title: Minimum points
minPoints.description: Only return stories/comments with at least this many points. WATCH MODE WARNING: if 'Also alert when a watched item hits a points/comments milestone' is on, any points milestone AT OR BELOW this value can never fire -- every item this query returns already has points >= this value the moment it first enters the baseline, so crossing a lower rung is impossible by construction. Drop those rungs from the milestones list or lower this value.

minComments.title: Minimum comments
minComments.description: Only return stories with at least this many comments (e.g. find high-engagement discussions). WATCH MODE WARNING: if 'Also alert when a watched item hits a points/comments milestone' is on, any comment-count milestone AT OR BELOW this value can never fire, same reason as Minimum points above.

excludeKeywords.title: Exclude keywords
excludeKeywords.description: Drop any story/comment whose title or text contains any of these words/phrases (case-insensitive). HN's search has no negative-term syntax, so this is applied to the matches after fetching, before you're charged -- e.g. queries:["rust"], excludeKeywords:["cryptocurrency"] keeps rust-the-language discussions and drops rust-the-crypto-project ones.

domainFilter.title: Domain filter
domainFilter.description: Only keep stories (and comments on those stories) whose linked URL's domain matches one of these, e.g. ["github.com","arxiv.org"] keeps github.com and any subdomain of it (api.github.com, gist.github.com, ...). Applied after fetching, before you're charged -- Algolia's search has no domain filter of its own. A comment is matched on its PARENT STORY's domain, since a comment has no URL of its own; items with no resolvable URL at all (text-only Ask HN posts, jobs) are dropped when this is set. Leave empty to keep every domain.

maxCommentDepth.title: Max comment depth
maxCommentDepth.description: Only keep comments this many hops or fewer from their story (1 = a direct reply to the story, 2 = a reply to a top-level comment, etc). Stories/jobs/polls are never affected. HN's search index has no depth field, so this is resolved by walking each comment's parent chain via HN's own Items API (one extra request per not-yet-resolved ancestor, cached across the run and shared between comments in the same thread). Every comment carries a commentDepth field, but it is only resolved (and only costs a lookup) when this is set -- leave empty and commentDepth stays null on every comment, at no extra cost. A lookup that fails or hits the per-run cap also leaves commentDepth:null for that comment and never drops it for an unknown depth.

author.title: Author username
author.description: Only return items posted by this exact HN username.

usernames.title: User profiles to look up
usernames.description: HN usernames to fetch profile data for (karma, about text, account creation date) — a separate lookup from the story/comment search above. To fetch ONLY user profiles with no story search, also set 'Search queries' and 'Filter by tag' to empty ([]).

postedBefore.title: Posted before (ISO date)
postedBefore.description: e.g. 2026-09-01. WATCH MODE WARNING: combined with watchLabel, a FIXED value here is a permanent dead end once the real date passes it — a newly-posted story/comment/job's own created-at is always "now", so no new item can ever be dated on or before an already-passed cutoff again. Leave it unset in a watched query; postedAfter alone is safe to keep. See README FAQ.

maxItemsPerQuery.title: Max items per query
maxItemsPerQuery.description: Cap per search query/tag combination. Hacker News' own search API never serves more than 1000 hits for one query, so without autoSplitLargeQueries anything above 1000 is clamped to 1000 (the run says so, and RUN_SUMMARY reports incompleteReason 'algolia-pagination-ceiling'). Turn autoSplitLargeQueries on to go past 1000.

autoSplitLargeQueries.title: Auto-split queries past the 1,000-hit ceiling
autoSplitLargeQueries.description: Hacker News' search API hands over at most 1000 hits per query however many matches it declares (a search for "ai" declares ~2 million and still returns 1000). Turn this on and any query that truncates is automatically re-searched in halved date windows until each window fits under the ceiling, so you get the full match set without working out the right slice width yourself. The windows are half-open and non-overlapping, so nothing is lost or counted twice at a boundary, and rows already returned by the wider pass are deduped -- you are never charged twice for the same item. Off by default: it re-searches the same query several times, which costs extra requests and run time you don't need for an ordinary capped pull. Pair it with a higher maxItemsPerQuery (its limit rises to 50000 once this is on) and watch maxResults/your charge limit.

maxSplitWindows.title: Max date windows per query (auto-split)
maxSplitWindows.description: With autoSplitLargeQueries: the most date windows one query may be halved into. Bounds the request count and run time of a very broad query. If a query is still truncated when the budget runs out, the run warns and RUN_SUMMARY reports splitExhausted: 'max-split-windows'. Minimum 3: the budget has to cover the first pass plus both halves of it, so 2 could never fit a single split.

watchLabel.title: Watch label (only new since last run)
watchLabel.description: Optional. Name a saved search (e.g. "my-launch-watch") and this run returns ONLY story/comment/job hits not delivered under that same label and filter set before, instead of the full match set every time. The first run for a label is a free baseline: it records what already matches (up to 5000 hits) and returns zero rows. Run it again later -- on a schedule, typically -- to get only what's new. The baseline is kept in your own Apify account (a named key-value store), keyed by label plus a fingerprint of queries/tags/author/sort/date-range/point-comment thresholds, so changing any of those starts a fresh baseline instead of dumping previously-excluded items as "new". Applies to the query/tag search only -- 'User profiles to look up' still runs and is charged normally every time, since a profile snapshot isn't a discrete new item.

watchChanges.title: Also alert when a watched item hits a points/comments milestone
watchChanges.description: Only used with a Watch label. By default watch mode alerts on brand-new items only: a story you were already delivered goes quiet forever, even if it later climbs to the front page, because its HN id never changes. Turn this on and an already-delivered item is re-delivered (and charged again, like a new row) when its points or comment count CROSSES one of the milestones below -- so you hear about a story breaking 100 or 500 points, not about every single upvote. Each milestone pays out at most once per item: a story crawling from 51 to 99 points over twenty scheduled runs returns nothing, then returns once when it reaches 100. Re-delivered rows carry _watchChangeType, _watchPrevious and _watchMilestone so you can see exactly what moved. Off by default.

watchPointMilestones.title: Points milestones
watchPointMilestones.description: Comma-separated point thresholds for the option above, e.g. "25,50,100,250,500,1000,2500,5000" (the default). Pick a ladder that matches your queries: Show HN and niche-tag watches rarely pass 100, while a front-page watch spends most of its life above it, and a ladder that is too fine re-charges you more often than you want. Leave EMPTY to disable points alerts and keep comment alerts only. Ignored unless the option above is on. WATCH MODE WARNING: any rung at or below 'Minimum points' can never fire -- see that field's description.

watchCommentMilestones.title: Comment-count milestones
watchCommentMilestones.description: Comma-separated comment-count thresholds, same rules as the points ladder above -- a discussion crossing 50 or 100 comments is usually the signal people watch for. Default "25,50,100,250,500,1000". Leave EMPTY to disable comment alerts and keep points alerts only. Ignored unless 'Also alert when a watched item hits a points/comments milestone' is on. WATCH MODE WARNING: any rung at or below 'Minimum comments' can never fire -- see that field's description.

enrichGithubLinks.title: Enrich GitHub links
enrichGithubLinks.description: When a story/comment's URL or text links to a GitHub repo (common on Show HN and technical discussions), looks it up on GitHub's public API and adds star count, primary language, last-push date, and open-issue count. Checks the item's own URL first, then its text, then its title -- for a comment (which has no URL of its own), that means the PARENT STORY's linked repo wins over any different repo the comment's own text names, whenever the story links to GitHub. Off by default -- adds one extra request per distinct repo found, bounded to 200 lookups per run against GitHub's unauthenticated 60/hour limit; repos already looked up earlier in the same run are cached, not re-fetched.

webhookUrl.title: Webhook URL (notify on completion)
webhookUrl.description: Optional. An http(s) URL to POST a small JSON summary to when the run finishes -- items pushed, hits scanned, and (when Watch label is set) whether this was a baseline run plus the new/skipped counts, along with the run's dataset ID so you can fetch the results. A convenience for callers who want a completion ping without setting up an Apify platform webhook (which needs separate Console/API configuration per Task, not per run). Best-effort: a failed or slow webhook is logged as a warning and never fails the run or affects charging -- it fires after every item has already been pushed and charged. Leave empty to skip.
